question: Why was the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil evaluated as a heat-transfer fluid higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with?
expect: premise false: 3.44 mg KOH/g is slightly lower than Goncalves (3.49) and much lower than Melo (12.24) and Amaral (12.8)
rendered:
The document "Thermophysical and Chemical Evaluation of Macaw Palm Almond Oil as a Biobased Heat-Transfer Fluid Candidate for Medium-Temperature Solar Thermal Applications" does not provide information that the acid value of the macaw palm almond oil was higher than every literature value for macaw oil it was compared with. 

In fact, the document states that the acid value measured for the oil was 3.44 ± 0.02 mg KOH·g−1, which is slightly lower than values reported by Gonçalves (3.49 mg KOH·g−1) and substantially lower than those of Melo (12.24 mg of KOH/g) and Amaral (12.8 mg KOH·g−1).
